title: Mirror Cuts
statement: A ribbon printed with lowercase letters must be cut into pieces so that every piece reads the same forwards and backwards. Return the smallest number of cuts needed. A ribbon that is already a palindrome needs 0 cuts.

examples.explanation: Two cuts: every letter on its own.

hints.content: Trying every way to cut is exponential.
Let cuts[i] be the fewest cuts for the first i letters. If text[j..i) is a palindrome, cuts[i] can be cuts[j] + 1.
Checking whether each substring is a palindrome from scratch adds another factor of n.
Expand around every center (each letter, and each gap between letters). Every palindrome text[l..r] found this way gives cuts[r + 1] = min(cuts[r + 1], cuts[l] + 1).
Start with cuts[i] = i - 1 (cut after every letter, with cuts[0] = -1 so a whole-prefix palindrome costs 0). The answer is cuts[n].

testCases.explanation: Two cuts: every letter on its own.
A single letter is a palindrome.
Three cuts: a | babbbab | b | ababa.
A long text that plain recursion cannot finish.

solutions.title: Try every first piece recursively
solutions.intuition: The first piece must be some palindromic prefix; try each and recurse on the rest.
solutions.approach: go(start) returns 0 if text[start..] is a palindrome; otherwise the minimum of 1 + go(end) over palindromic pieces text[start..end).
solutions.pseudocode: go(s): if pal(t[s..]): return 0; return min over e in s+1..n-1 with pal(t[s..e)) of 1 + go(e)
commonMistakes: Counting pieces instead of cuts (off by one).
solutions.interviewExplanation: This enumerates every partition. The same suffixes are re-solved many times, so it's exponential without memoization.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: 'aab' is not a palindrome. Piece 'a' leaves 'ab' (1 cut + 1 more); piece 'aa' leaves 'b', a palindrome.

solutions.title: Center expansion with a cuts table
solutions.intuition: Every palindrome is found once by expanding from its center, and each one offers a way to end a prefix with one more cut.
solutions.approach: cuts[i] = i - 1 for i in 0..n. For each center, expand odd and even palindromes; for each text[l..r] found, update cuts[r + 1] = min(cuts[r + 1], cuts[l] + 1). Return cuts[n].
solutions.pseudocode:
cuts[i] = i - 1
for c in 0..n-1: for (l, r) in [(c, c), (c, c+1)]: while in range and t[l] == t[r]: cuts[r+1] = min(cuts[r+1], cuts[l] + 1); l--; r++
return cuts[n]
commonMistakes: Initializing cuts[0] to 0 instead of -1, which charges a cut for a prefix that is itself a palindrome.
solutions.interviewExplanation: cuts[i] is the fewest cuts for the first i letters, with cuts[0] = -1 as a sentinel. Expanding around all 2n - 1 centers discovers every palindrome text[l..r] in O(n²) total, and each one relaxes cuts[r + 1] from cuts[l] + 1. That avoids the separate O(n²) palindrome table and runs in O(n²) time with O(n) memory.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: 'b' alone → cuts[3] = cuts[2] + 1 = 1. The answer is 1.
